nodes.title: Rough running with a current cylinder-one misfire finding
nodes.entry_criteria:
## G1.1 Entry and distinction from other guidance

Use this procedure when rough running is accompanied by a current scan
recording the exact code P0301. That finding establishes a cylinder-one
misfire report; it does not establish a failed ignition component.

Rough idle or a warning light alone does not distinguish this procedure from
[SG-02](SG-02-lean-idle.md). Ask for the current scan finding before selecting
between them. A historical P0171 report does not override a current P0301
record. P03010 is not P0301.

If both P0301 and P0171 are current, these three guides do not establish which
procedure takes priority. Clarify with the workshop; do not assume code
priority or claim that one code explains the other.

If the symptom or current finding is different, do not force it into this
procedure. Request clarification or report that the supplied guides do not
cover the established complaint.

nodes.description: Review the recorded coil comparison
nodes.instruction:
## G1.2 Review the recorded coil comparison

At the entry state, the next action is to review the workshop's completed,
controlled ignition-coil comparison record.

An interpretable comparison identifies:

- The current job, the original P0301 finding and the donor cylinder.
- A baseline observation reproducing the original finding.
- A coil-only change, with the plug and other diagnostic variables unchanged.
- The observed cylinder after that change.
- A return-to-original comparison reproducing the baseline finding.

For this fictional guide, the published result categories are:

| Recorded result | Permitted transition |
| --- | --- |
| The misfire follows the cylinder-one coil to the donor cylinder, and returning the coils reproduces P0301 | Terminal finding in G1.4: cylinder-one ignition-coil fault |
| The misfire remains on cylinder one during a valid coil comparison and after the return check | Continue to the plug-record review in G1.3; a coil fault has not been established |
| No coil-comparison record is supplied, or the check was not done | Stop with the coil-record review as the next action |
| A supplied comparison lacks a required control or observation, or is inconclusive | Clarify at this action; do not take either result branch |
| Records of the same coil comparison disagree about what changed or which cylinder misfired | Clarify at this action; do not merge the records into a diagnosis |

The phrase "no change after substitution" is insufficient by itself. It must
be attributable to a coil-only comparison for this job with the required
controls. A parts recommendation or replacement invoice is not that evidence.

Use only records for the declared vehicle, current job and requested profile. A supplied wrong-vehicle record requires clarification, not a result.

nodes.description: The completed coil-only comparison leaves the misfire on cylinder one.
Review the recorded plug comparison
nodes.instruction:
## G1.3 Review the recorded plug comparison

This action is available only after the valid coil comparison leaves the
misfire on cylinder one. A statement that the plug has not been checked means
this action remains outstanding, not that the plug passed or failed.

The plug comparison uses the same record requirements as G1.2, except that
the plug is the only changed diagnostic variable and the coils are in their
original positions. Its baseline must still reproduce P0301.

| Recorded result | Permitted transition |
| --- | --- |
| The misfire follows the cylinder-one plug to the donor cylinder, and returning the plugs reproduces P0301 | Terminal finding in G1.4: cylinder-one spark-plug fault |
| The misfire remains on cylinder one in the completed comparison | Continue to the workshop-review action in G1.5 |
| The record is not supplied or explicitly says the check was not done | Stop with the plug-record review as the next action |
| A supplied record is partial, contradictory or inconclusive | Clarify at the plug-record review |

Use only records for the declared vehicle, current job and requested profile. A supplied wrong-vehicle record requires clarification, not a result.

nodes.description: Review the current RP-IDLE pressure record
nodes.instruction:
## G2.2 Review the current pressure record

The next action is to review the saved workshop pressure record for profile
RP-IDLE: the current complaint reproduced at running idle for the declared
job. A valid record identifies that profile, the job, the value and the unit.

For this fictional profile only, the reference band is 250 through 400 kPa,
including both boundaries. The documented unit conversion is 1 bar = 100 kPa;
therefore a correctly scoped 3.1 bar record means 310 kPa.
Do not invent a unit for "3.1" or apply an undocumented conversion.

| Recorded result | Permitted transition |
| --- | --- |
| A complete current RP-IDLE record is inside the inclusive band | Continue to the localisation-record review in G2.3 |
| A complete current RP-IDLE record is outside the band | Request workshop review of the out-of-band pressure finding; no component cause is established |
| No pressure record has been supplied or the check was not done | Stop with this pressure-record review as the next action |
| A supplied record lacks the unit or profile, or equally applicable records conflict | Clarify at this action |

An old low reading, a crossed-out value or a measurement taken in a different
operating profile does not override the applicable RP-IDLE record. Conversely,
do not discard two conflicting applicable records merely by choosing the
more convenient value. Ask the workshop to resolve the conflict.

Being inside the reference band does not prove that the vehicle has no fault.
It only permits the next published action in this guide.

Use only records for the declared vehicle, current job and requested profile. A supplied wrong-vehicle record requires clarification, not a result.

nodes.description: The current RP-IDLE pressure record is within the source reference band.
Review the complete joint J localisation record
nodes.instruction:
## G2.3 Review the controlled localisation record

This action is available after the current pressure record is within band.
It reviews the workshop's controlled record for the designated intake joint J.
Joint J is a named location in this procedure, not a general component
taxonomy or a physical-topology subgraph.

A complete record identifies the same job, the same reproduced complaint
and profile RP-IDLE, no other diagnostic changes, and all four observations:

| Observation | Fictional criterion |
| --- | --- |
| A: original configuration | Recorded correction exceeds +15% |
| B: joint J isolated in the workshop comparison | Recorded correction is between -5% and +5%, inclusive |
| A2: original configuration restored | Recorded correction again exceeds +15% |
| C: comparison control at joint K, with J in its original configuration | Recorded correction exceeds +15% |

Here "correction" is the percentage field explicitly identified in the
workshop report. These invented bands define only this source's category.
Do not substitute a different percentage field, operating profile or job.

If all four criteria are met and pressure remains within its reference band
throughout the comparison, take the repeatable-localisation result to G2.4.
A separately signed pressure-stability statement for the comparison is
acceptable; pressure values need not be repeated in every row.

If the completed, otherwise valid record fails to reproduce the pattern,
take the non-localising result to the workshop-review action in G2.5.
If a required observation or control is missing, the supplied record is
incomplete: clarify at this action rather than treating it as non-localising.
If the record explicitly says the entire comparison was not done, leave this
review as the next action.

A single improvement in B is not enough. In particular, a low correction
that remains low after restoring A does not localise the fault to J.

Use only records for the declared vehicle, current job and requested profile. A supplied wrong-vehicle record requires clarification, not a result.

nodes.description: Review the current workshop fan-stage record
nodes.instruction:
## G3.2 Review the fan-stage record

The first action is to review the current workshop record of airflow at the
four commanded fan stages. The customer complaint can identify the relevant
guide, but it does not substitute for this workshop observation.

| Current workshop record | Permitted transition |
| --- | --- |
| No airflow at stages 1, 2 and 3; airflow present at stage 4 | Continue to the low-speed control comparison in G3.3 |
| No airflow at any stage | Request workshop review of complete airflow loss; no component cause is established |
| Airflow is present at every stage and the remaining complaint is air temperature | Refer outside this airflow procedure; no component diagnosis is established |
| Another complete speed pattern | Request workshop review of a pattern not covered by this guide |
| No workshop stage record exists or the check was not done | Stop with the fan-stage record review as the next action |
| A supplied stage record is partial or internally contradictory | Clarify at this action |

A successful stage 4 is not proof that the low-speed controller has failed.
An all-stages airflow record is not proof that the customer's temperature
complaint has no cause.

Use only records for the declared vehicle, current job and requested profile. A supplied wrong-vehicle record requires clarification, not a result.

nodes.description: Current workshop record: stages 1-3 have no airflow; stage 4 has airflow.
Review the completed CP-FAN control-unit comparison
nodes.instruction:
## G3.3 Review the low-speed control comparison

The next action is to review the workshop's completed controlled comparison.
For the fictional reference procedure CP-FAN, an interpretable record states:

- It concerns the same current job and reproduced fan-stage pattern.
- The workshop's supply, ground and connection-integrity checks met CP-FAN
  requirements throughout the comparison.
- The low-speed control unit was the only changed diagnostic variable.
- A: with the original unit, stages 1-3 have no airflow and stage 4 has airflow.
- B: with the reference unit, airflow is present at all four stages.
- A2: with the original unit restored, the original 1-3/4 pattern recurs.

CP-FAN is a fictional record-review protocol, not an electrical procedure.
This document supplies no real test limits or physical test instructions.
A report can state that its protocol checks passed; a model must not invent
that statement or infer it solely from the fan-stage pattern.

| Recorded result | Permitted transition |
| --- | --- |
| The complete comparison meets all criteria above | Terminal finding in G3.4 |
| A complete, otherwise valid comparison does not reproduce the A-B-A2 pattern | Request workshop review of unresolved low-speed airflow loss |
| The comparison was not done or no comparison record has been supplied | Leave this comparison-record review as the next action |
| A comparison is supplied but the return check, protocol prerequisites or another required observation is missing | Clarify at this action |
| Observations or the identity of the changed unit conflict | Clarify at this action |

Do not name a failed unit from B alone. The return comparison prevents a
single coincidental improvement from becoming the terminal conclusion.

Use only records for the declared vehicle, current job and requested profile. A supplied wrong-vehicle record requires clarification, not a result.

nodes.description: Review the current RP-IDLE pressure record
nodes.instruction:
## G2.2 Review the current pressure record

The next action is to review the saved workshop pressure record for profile
RP-IDLE: the current complaint reproduced at running idle for the declared
job. A valid record identifies that profile, the job, the value and the unit.

For this fictional profile only, the reference band is 450 through 600 kPa,
including both boundaries. The documented unit conversion is 1 bar = 100 kPa;
therefore a correctly scoped 5.25 bar record means 525 kPa.
Do not invent a unit for "5.25" or apply an undocumented conversion.

| Recorded result | Permitted transition |
| --- | --- |
| A complete current RP-IDLE record is inside the inclusive band | Continue to the localisation-record review in G2.3 |
| A complete current RP-IDLE record is outside the band | Request workshop review of the out-of-band pressure finding; no component cause is established |
| No pressure record has been supplied or the check was not done | Stop with this pressure-record review as the next action |
| A supplied record lacks the unit or profile, or equally applicable records conflict | Clarify at this action |

An old low reading, a crossed-out value or a measurement taken in a different
operating profile does not override the applicable RP-IDLE record. Conversely,
do not discard two conflicting applicable records merely by choosing the
more convenient value. Ask the workshop to resolve the conflict.

Being inside the reference band does not prove that the vehicle has no fault.
It only permits the next published action in this guide.

nodes.instruction:
## G2.3 Review the controlled localisation record

This action is available after the current pressure record is within band.
It reviews the workshop's controlled record for the designated intake joint L.
Joint L is a named location in this procedure, not a general component
taxonomy or a physical-topology subgraph.

A complete record identifies the same job, the same reproduced complaint
and profile RP-IDLE, no other diagnostic changes, and all four observations:

| Observation | Fictional criterion |
| --- | --- |
| A: original configuration | Recorded correction exceeds +15% |
| B: joint L isolated in the workshop comparison | Recorded correction is between -5% and +5%, inclusive |
| A2: original configuration restored | Recorded correction again exceeds +15% |
| C: comparison control at joint K, with L in its original configuration | Recorded correction exceeds +15% |

Here "correction" is the percentage field explicitly identified in the
workshop report. These invented bands define only this source's category.
Do not substitute a different percentage field, operating profile or job.

If all four criteria are met and pressure remains within its reference band
throughout the comparison, take the repeatable-localisation result to G2.4.
A separately signed pressure-stability statement for the comparison is
acceptable; pressure values need not be repeated in every row.

If the completed, otherwise valid record fails to reproduce the pattern,
take the non-localising result to the workshop-review action in G2.5.
If a required observation or control is missing, the supplied record is
incomplete: clarify at this action rather than treating it as non-localising.
If the record explicitly says the entire comparison was not done, leave this
review as the next action.

A single improvement in B is not enough. In particular, a low correction
that remains low after restoring A does not localise the fault to L.

Use only records for the declared vehicle, current job and requested profile. A supplied wrong-vehicle record requires clarification, not a result.

nodes.description: Review the recorded coil comparison
nodes.instruction:
## G1.2 Review the recorded coil comparison

At the entry state, the next action is to review the workshop's completed,
controlled ignition-coil comparison record.

An interpretable comparison identifies:

- The current job, the original P0302 finding and the donor cylinder.
- A baseline observation reproducing the original finding.
- A coil-only change, with the plug and other diagnostic variables unchanged.
- The observed cylinder after that change.
- A return-to-original comparison reproducing the baseline finding.

For this fictional guide, the published result categories are:

| Recorded result | Permitted transition |
| --- | --- |
| The misfire follows the cylinder-two coil to the donor cylinder, and returning the coils reproduces P0302 | Terminal finding in G1.4: cylinder-two ignition-coil fault |
| The misfire remains on cylinder two during a valid coil comparison and after the return check | Continue to the plug-record review in G1.3; a coil fault has not been established |
| No coil-comparison record is supplied, or the check was not done | Stop with the coil-record review as the next action |
| A supplied comparison lacks a required control or observation, or is inconclusive | Clarify at this action; do not take either result branch |
| Records of the same coil comparison disagree about what changed or which cylinder misfired | Clarify at this action; do not merge the records into a diagnosis |

The phrase "no change after substitution" is insufficient by itself. It must
be attributable to a coil-only comparison for this job with the required
controls. A parts recommendation or replacement invoice is not that evidence.

Use only records for the declared vehicle, current job and requested profile. A supplied wrong-vehicle record requires clarification, not a result.

nodes.description: Review the current RP-IDLE pressure record
nodes.instruction:
## G2.2 Review the current pressure record

The next action is to review the saved workshop pressure record for profile
RP-IDLE: the current complaint reproduced at running idle for the declared
job. A valid record identifies that profile, the job, the value and the unit.

For this fictional profile only, the reference band is 300 through 450 kPa,
including both boundaries. The documented unit conversion is 1 bar = 100 kPa;
therefore a correctly scoped 3.75 bar record means 375 kPa.
Do not invent a unit for "3.75" or apply an undocumented conversion.

| Recorded result | Permitted transition |
| --- | --- |
| A complete current RP-IDLE record is inside the inclusive band | Continue to the localisation-record review in G2.3 |
| A complete current RP-IDLE record is outside the band | Request workshop review of the out-of-band pressure finding; no component cause is established |
| No pressure record has been supplied or the check was not done | Stop with this pressure-record review as the next action |
| A supplied record lacks the unit or profile, or equally applicable records conflict | Clarify at this action |

An old low reading, a crossed-out value or a measurement taken in a different
operating profile does not override the applicable RP-IDLE record. Conversely,
do not discard two conflicting applicable records merely by choosing the
more convenient value. Ask the workshop to resolve the conflict.

Being inside the reference band does not prove that the vehicle has no fault.
It only permits the next published action in this guide.

Use only records for the declared vehicle, current job and requested profile. A supplied wrong-vehicle record requires clarification, not a result.

Review the complete joint M localisation record
nodes.instruction:
## G2.3 Review the controlled localisation record

This action is available after the current pressure record is within band.
It reviews the workshop's controlled record for the designated intake joint M.
Joint M is a named location in this procedure, not a general component
taxonomy or a physical-topology subgraph.

A complete record identifies the same job, the same reproduced complaint
and profile RP-IDLE, no other diagnostic changes, and all four observations:

| Observation | Fictional criterion |
| --- | --- |
| A: original configuration | Recorded correction exceeds +15% |
| B: joint M isolated in the workshop comparison | Recorded correction is between -5% and +5%, inclusive |
| A2: original configuration restored | Recorded correction again exceeds +15% |
| C: comparison control at joint K, with M in its original configuration | Recorded correction exceeds +15% |

Here "correction" is the percentage field explicitly identified in the
workshop report. These invented bands define only this source's category.
Do not substitute a different percentage field, operating profile or job.

If all four criteria are met and pressure remains within its reference band
throughout the comparison, take the repeatable-localisation result to G2.4.
A separately signed pressure-stability statement for the comparison is
acceptable; pressure values need not be repeated in every row.

If the completed, otherwise valid record fails to reproduce the pattern,
take the non-localising result to the workshop-review action in G2.5.
If a required observation or control is missing, the supplied record is
incomplete: clarify at this action rather than treating it as non-localising.
If the record explicitly says the entire comparison was not done, leave this
review as the next action.

A single improvement in B is not enough. In particular, a low correction
that remains low after restoring A does not localise the fault to M.

Use only records for the declared vehicle, current job and requested profile. A supplied wrong-vehicle record requires clarification, not a result.

nodes.description: Review the current RP-IDLE pressure record
nodes.instruction:
## G2.2 Review the current pressure record

The next action is to review the saved workshop pressure record for profile
RP-IDLE: the current complaint reproduced at running idle for the declared
job. A valid record identifies that profile, the job, the value and the unit.

For this fictional profile only, the reference band is 500 through 650 kPa,
including both boundaries. The documented unit conversion is 1 bar = 100 kPa;
therefore a correctly scoped 5.75 bar record means 575 kPa.
Do not invent a unit for "5.75" or apply an undocumented conversion.

| Recorded result | Permitted transition |
| --- | --- |
| A complete current RP-IDLE record is inside the inclusive band | Continue to the localisation-record review in G2.3 |
| A complete current RP-IDLE record is outside the band | Request workshop review of the out-of-band pressure finding; no component cause is established |
| No pressure record has been supplied or the check was not done | Stop with this pressure-record review as the next action |
| A supplied record lacks the unit or profile, or equally applicable records conflict | Clarify at this action |

An old low reading, a crossed-out value or a measurement taken in a different
operating profile does not override the applicable RP-IDLE record. Conversely,
do not discard two conflicting applicable records merely by choosing the
more convenient value. Ask the workshop to resolve the conflict.

Being inside the reference band does not prove that the vehicle has no fault.
It only permits the next published action in this guide.

Review the complete joint N localisation record
nodes.instruction:
## G2.3 Review the controlled localisation record

This action is available after the current pressure record is within band.
It reviews the workshop's controlled record for the designated intake joint N.
Joint N is a named location in this procedure, not a general component
taxonomy or a physical-topology subgraph.

A complete record identifies the same job, the same reproduced complaint
and profile RP-IDLE, no other diagnostic changes, and all four observations:

| Observation | Fictional criterion |
| --- | --- |
| A: original configuration | Recorded correction exceeds +15% |
| B: joint N isolated in the workshop comparison | Recorded correction is between -5% and +5%, inclusive |
| A2: original configuration restored | Recorded correction again exceeds +15% |
| C: comparison control at joint K, with N in its original configuration | Recorded correction exceeds +15% |

Here "correction" is the percentage field explicitly identified in the
workshop report. These invented bands define only this source's category.
Do not substitute a different percentage field, operating profile or job.

If all four criteria are met and pressure remains within its reference band
throughout the comparison, take the repeatable-localisation result to G2.4.
A separately signed pressure-stability statement for the comparison is
acceptable; pressure values need not be repeated in every row.

If the completed, otherwise valid record fails to reproduce the pattern,
take the non-localising result to the workshop-review action in G2.5.
If a required observation or control is missing, the supplied record is
incomplete: clarify at this action rather than treating it as non-localising.
If the record explicitly says the entire comparison was not done, leave this
review as the next action.

A single improvement in B is not enough. In particular, a low correction
that remains low after restoring A does not localise the fault to N.

Use only records for the declared vehicle, current job and requested profile. A supplied wrong-vehicle record requires clarification, not a result.

nodes.description: Review the recorded coil comparison
nodes.instruction:
## G1.2 Review the recorded coil comparison

At the entry state, the next action is to review the workshop's completed,
controlled ignition-coil comparison record.

An interpretable comparison identifies:

- The current job, the original P0301 finding and the donor cylinder.
- A baseline observation reproducing the original finding.
- A coil-only change, with the plug and other diagnostic variables unchanged.
- The observed cylinder after that change.
- A return-to-original comparison reproducing the baseline finding.

For this fictional guide, the published result categories are:

| Recorded result | Permitted transition |
| --- | --- |
| The misfire follows the cylinder-one coil to the donor cylinder, and returning the coils reproduces P0301 | Terminal finding in G1.4: cylinder-one ignition-coil fault |
| The misfire remains on cylinder one during a valid coil comparison and after the return check | Continue to the plug-record review in G1.3; a coil fault has not been established |
| No coil-comparison record is supplied, or the check was not done | Stop with the coil-record review as the next action |
| A supplied comparison lacks a required control or observation, or is inconclusive | Clarify at this action; do not take either result branch |
| Records of the same coil comparison disagree about what changed or which cylinder misfired | Clarify at this action; do not merge the records into a diagnosis |

The phrase "no change after substitution" is insufficient by itself. It must
be attributable to a coil-only comparison for this job with the required
controls. A parts recommendation or replacement invoice is not that evidence.

Use only records for the declared vehicle, current job and requested profile. A supplied wrong-vehicle record requires clarification, not a result.

nodes.description: Review the current RP-IDLE pressure record
nodes.instruction:
## G2.2 Review the current pressure record

The next action is to review the saved workshop pressure record for profile
RP-IDLE: the current complaint reproduced at running idle for the declared
job. A valid record identifies that profile, the job, the value and the unit.

For this fictional profile only, the reference band is 275 through 375 kPa,
including both boundaries. The documented unit conversion is 1 bar = 100 kPa;
therefore a correctly scoped 3.25 bar record means 325 kPa.
Do not invent a unit for "3.25" or apply an undocumented conversion.

| Recorded result | Permitted transition |
| --- | --- |
| A complete current RP-IDLE record is inside the inclusive band | Continue to the localisation-record review in G2.3 |
| A complete current RP-IDLE record is outside the band | Request workshop review of the out-of-band pressure finding; no component cause is established |
| No pressure record has been supplied or the check was not done | Stop with this pressure-record review as the next action |
| A supplied record lacks the unit or profile, or equally applicable records conflict | Clarify at this action |

An old low reading, a crossed-out value or a measurement taken in a different
operating profile does not override the applicable RP-IDLE record. Conversely,
do not discard two conflicting applicable records merely by choosing the
more convenient value. Ask the workshop to resolve the conflict.

Being inside the reference band does not prove that the vehicle has no fault.
It only permits the next published action in this guide.

Use only records for the declared vehicle, current job and requested profile. A supplied wrong-vehicle record requires clarification, not a result.

nodes.instruction:
## G2.3 Review the controlled localisation record

This action is available after the current pressure record is within band.
It reviews the workshop's controlled record for the designated intake joint P.
Joint P is a named location in this procedure, not a general component
taxonomy or a physical-topology subgraph.

A complete record identifies the same job, the same reproduced complaint
and profile RP-IDLE, no other diagnostic changes, and all four observations:

| Observation | Fictional criterion |
| --- | --- |
| A: original configuration | Recorded correction exceeds +15% |
| B: joint P isolated in the workshop comparison | Recorded correction is between -5% and +5%, inclusive |
| A2: original configuration restored | Recorded correction again exceeds +15% |
| C: comparison control at joint K, with P in its original configuration | Recorded correction exceeds +15% |

Here "correction" is the percentage field explicitly identified in the
workshop report. These invented bands define only this source's category.
Do not substitute a different percentage field, operating profile or job.

If all four criteria are met and pressure remains within its reference band
throughout the comparison, take the repeatable-localisation result to G2.4.
A separately signed pressure-stability statement for the comparison is
acceptable; pressure values need not be repeated in every row.

If the completed, otherwise valid record fails to reproduce the pattern,
take the non-localising result to the workshop-review action in G2.5.
If a required observation or control is missing, the supplied record is
incomplete: clarify at this action rather than treating it as non-localising.
If the record explicitly says the entire comparison was not done, leave this
review as the next action.

A single improvement in B is not enough. In particular, a low correction
that remains low after restoring A does not localise the fault to P.

Use only records for the declared vehicle, current job and requested profile. A supplied wrong-vehicle record requires clarification, not a result.

## G1.1 Entry and distinction from other guidance

Use this procedure when rough running is accompanied by a current scan
recording the exact code P0302. That finding establishes a cylinder-two
misfire report; it does not establish a failed ignition component.

between them. A historical P0171 report does not override a current P0302
record. P03020 is not P0302.

If both P0302 and P0171 are current, these three guides do not establish which
procedure takes priority. Clarify with the workshop; do not assume code
priority or claim that one code explains the other.

If the symptom or current finding is different, do not force it into this
procedure. Request clarification or report that the supplied guides do not
cover the established complaint.

## G4.0 Provenance, applicability and precedence

This supplement extends SG-01, SG-02 and SG-03 to the ten configurations below.
It is authored fictional guidance, not manufacturer information or expert-
validated advice. All numbers, protocols and component findings are invented.

review order or fan-stage pattern from a neighbouring configuration.

## G4.2 Misfire variants

number. The donor code is P030 followed by its donor number. The base guide's
"cylinder one" references mean the scheduled cylinder instead. Exact code
matching still applies: an extra digit is not the same finding.

complete coil comparison leaves the misfire on the original cylinder.
Plug-first rows instead use the review instructions in G4.3 and G4.4.

that component finding. If it remains on the original cylinder, review the
second component. If both complete comparisons remain on that cylinder,
refer for unresolved misfire; do not invent another component conclusion.
Never reuse controls from one comparison as evidence that the other was done.

nodes.description: Review the recorded coil comparison
nodes.instruction:
## G1.2 Review the recorded coil comparison

At the entry state, the next action is to review the workshop's completed,
controlled ignition-coil comparison record.

An interpretable comparison identifies:

- The current job, the original P0302 finding and the donor cylinder.
- A baseline observation reproducing the original finding.
- A coil-only change, with the plug and other diagnostic variables unchanged.
- The observed cylinder after that change.
- A return-to-original comparison reproducing the baseline finding.

For this fictional guide, the published result categories are:

| Recorded result | Permitted transition |
| --- | --- |
| The misfire follows the cylinder-two coil to the donor cylinder, and returning the coils reproduces P0302 | Terminal finding in G1.4: cylinder-two ignition-coil fault |
| The misfire remains on cylinder two during a valid coil comparison and after the return check | Continue to the plug-record review in G1.3; a coil fault has not been established |
| No coil-comparison record is supplied, or the check was not done | Stop with the coil-record review as the next action |
| A supplied comparison lacks a required control or observation, or is inconclusive | Clarify at this action; do not take either result branch |
| Records of the same coil comparison disagree about what changed or which cylinder misfired | Clarify at this action; do not merge the records into a diagnosis |

The phrase "no change after substitution" is insufficient by itself. It must
be attributable to a coil-only comparison for this job with the required
controls. A parts recommendation or replacement invoice is not that evidence.

Use only records for the declared vehicle, current job and requested profile. A supplied wrong-vehicle record requires clarification, not a result.

| The misfire remains on cylinder two in the completed comparison | Continue to the workshop-review action in G1.5 |
| The record is not supplied or explicitly says the check was not done | Stop with the plug-record review as the next action |
| A supplied record is partial, contradictory or inconclusive | Clarify at the plug-record review |

nodes.description: Review the current RP-IDLE pressure record
nodes.instruction:
## G2.2 Review the current pressure record

The next action is to review the saved workshop pressure record for profile
RP-IDLE: the current complaint reproduced at running idle for the declared
job. A valid record identifies that profile, the job, the value and the unit.

For this fictional profile only, the reference band is 400 through 550 kPa,
including both boundaries. The documented unit conversion is 1 bar = 100 kPa;
therefore a correctly scoped 4.75 bar record means 475 kPa.
Do not invent a unit for "4.75" or apply an undocumented conversion.

| Recorded result | Permitted transition |
| --- | --- |
| A complete current RP-IDLE record is inside the inclusive band | Continue to the localisation-record review in G2.3 |
| A complete current RP-IDLE record is outside the band | Request workshop review of the out-of-band pressure finding; no component cause is established |
| No pressure record has been supplied or the check was not done | Stop with this pressure-record review as the next action |
| A supplied record lacks the unit or profile, or equally applicable records conflict | Clarify at this action |

An old low reading, a crossed-out value or a measurement taken in a different
operating profile does not override the applicable RP-IDLE record. Conversely,
do not discard two conflicting applicable records merely by choosing the
more convenient value. Ask the workshop to resolve the conflict.

Being inside the reference band does not prove that the vehicle has no fault.
It only permits the next published action in this guide.

Use only records for the declared vehicle, current job and requested profile. A supplied wrong-vehicle record requires clarification, not a result.

Review the complete joint Q localisation record
nodes.instruction:
## G2.3 Review the controlled localisation record

This action is available after the current pressure record is within band.
It reviews the workshop's controlled record for the designated intake joint Q.
Joint Q is a named location in this procedure, not a general component
taxonomy or a physical-topology subgraph.

A complete record identifies the same job, the same reproduced complaint
and profile RP-IDLE, no other diagnostic changes, and all four observations:

| Observation | Fictional criterion |
| --- | --- |
| A: original configuration | Recorded correction exceeds +15% |
| B: joint Q isolated in the workshop comparison | Recorded correction is between -5% and +5%, inclusive |
| A2: original configuration restored | Recorded correction again exceeds +15% |
| C: comparison control at joint K, with Q in its original configuration | Recorded correction exceeds +15% |

Here "correction" is the percentage field explicitly identified in the
workshop report. These invented bands define only this source's category.
Do not substitute a different percentage field, operating profile or job.

If all four criteria are met and pressure remains within its reference band
throughout the comparison, take the repeatable-localisation result to G2.4.
A separately signed pressure-stability statement for the comparison is
acceptable; pressure values need not be repeated in every row.

If the completed, otherwise valid record fails to reproduce the pattern,
take the non-localising result to the workshop-review action in G2.5.
If a required observation or control is missing, the supplied record is
incomplete: clarify at this action rather than treating it as non-localising.
If the record explicitly says the entire comparison was not done, leave this
review as the next action.

A single improvement in B is not enough. In particular, a low correction
that remains low after restoring A does not localise the fault to Q.

Use only records for the declared vehicle, current job and requested profile. A supplied wrong-vehicle record requires clarification, not a result.

nodes.entry_criteria:
## G1.1 Entry and distinction from other guidance

Use this procedure when rough running is accompanied by a current scan
recording the exact code P0303. That finding establishes a cylinder-three
misfire report; it does not establish a failed ignition component.

Rough idle or a warning light alone does not distinguish this procedure from
[SG-02](SG-02-lean-idle.md). Ask for the current scan finding before selecting
between them. A historical P0171 report does not override a current P0303
record. P03030 is not P0303.

If both P0303 and P0171 are current, these three guides do not establish which
procedure takes priority. Clarify with the workshop; do not assume code
priority or claim that one code explains the other.

If the symptom or current finding is different, do not force it into this
procedure. Request clarification or report that the supplied guides do not
cover the established complaint.

## G4.0 Provenance, applicability and precedence

This supplement extends SG-01, SG-02 and SG-03 to the ten configurations below.
It is authored fictional guidance, not manufacturer information or expert-
validated advice. All numbers, protocols and component findings are invented.
Review supplied workshop records only; do not perform vehicle work.

Each row is an exact applicability boundary, not a family-wide approval.
The original three guides remain unchanged for row a21. For the other rows,
use the base guide's evidence controls with this supplement's explicit
substitutions and ordering. Never transfer a pressure band, cylinder finding,
review order or fan-stage pattern from a neighbouring configuration.
No priorities between simultaneous current misfire and lean findings are given.

Model, year and configuration must be established. Missing identity requires
clarification even if the catalogue currently lists only one matching model.
An explicitly unsupported configuration is unsupported, not the nearest match.
If a selected vehicle and the report disagree, clarify the conflict rather than
silently choosing either one. A missing selection does not establish identity.
Vehicle/job/profile identifiers on workshop records must match the current case.
Historical or explicitly different-vehicle records cannot establish a transition.

## G4.2 Misfire variants

For each configuration the exact entry code is P030 followed by its cylinder
number. The donor code is P030 followed by its donor number. The base guide's
"cylinder one" references mean the scheduled cylinder instead. Exact code
matching still applies: an extra digit is not the same finding.

Coil-first rows use SG-01's order: coil review, then plug review only if the
complete coil comparison leaves the misfire on the original cylinder.
Plug-first rows instead use the review instructions in G4.3 and G4.4.
The first comparison following the component with a valid return establishes
that component finding. If it remains on the original cylinder, review the
second component. If both complete comparisons remain on that cylinder,
refer for unresolved misfire; do not invent another component conclusion.
Never reuse controls from one comparison as evidence that the other was done.

nodes.description: Review the recorded coil comparison
nodes.instruction:
## G1.2 Review the recorded coil comparison

At the entry state, the next action is to review the workshop's completed,
controlled ignition-coil comparison record.

An interpretable comparison identifies:

- The current job, the original P0303 finding and the donor cylinder.
- A baseline observation reproducing the original finding.
- A coil-only change, with the plug and other diagnostic variables unchanged.
- The observed cylinder after that change.
- A return-to-original comparison reproducing the baseline finding.

For this fictional guide, the published result categories are:

| Recorded result | Permitted transition |
| --- | --- |
| The misfire follows the cylinder-three coil to the donor cylinder, and returning the coils reproduces P0303 | Terminal finding in G1.4: cylinder-three ignition-coil fault |
| The misfire remains on cylinder three during a valid coil comparison and after the return check | Continue to the plug-record review in G1.3; a coil fault has not been established |
| No coil-comparison record is supplied, or the check was not done | Stop with the coil-record review as the next action |
| A supplied comparison lacks a required control or observation, or is inconclusive | Clarify at this action; do not take either result branch |
| Records of the same coil comparison disagree about what changed or which cylinder misfired | Clarify at this action; do not merge the records into a diagnosis |

The phrase "no change after substitution" is insufficient by itself. It must
be attributable to a coil-only comparison for this job with the required
controls. A parts recommendation or replacement invoice is not that evidence.

Use only records for the declared vehicle, current job and requested profile. A supplied wrong-vehicle record requires clarification, not a result.

nodes.description: Review the current RP-IDLE pressure record
nodes.instruction:
## G2.2 Review the current pressure record

The next action is to review the saved workshop pressure record for profile
RP-IDLE: the current complaint reproduced at running idle for the declared
job. A valid record identifies that profile, the job, the value and the unit.

For this fictional profile only, the reference band is 350 through 500 kPa,
including both boundaries. The documented unit conversion is 1 bar = 100 kPa;
therefore a correctly scoped 4.25 bar record means 425 kPa.
Do not invent a unit for "4.25" or apply an undocumented conversion.

| Recorded result | Permitted transition |
| --- | --- |
| A complete current RP-IDLE record is inside the inclusive band | Continue to the localisation-record review in G2.3 |
| A complete current RP-IDLE record is outside the band | Request workshop review of the out-of-band pressure finding; no component cause is established |
| No pressure record has been supplied or the check was not done | Stop with this pressure-record review as the next action |
| A supplied record lacks the unit or profile, or equally applicable records conflict | Clarify at this action |

An old low reading, a crossed-out value or a measurement taken in a different
operating profile does not override the applicable RP-IDLE record. Conversely,
do not discard two conflicting applicable records merely by choosing the
more convenient value. Ask the workshop to resolve the conflict.

Being inside the reference band does not prove that the vehicle has no fault.
It only permits the next published action in this guide.

Review the complete joint R localisation record
nodes.instruction:
## G2.3 Review the controlled localisation record

This action is available after the current pressure record is within band.
It reviews the workshop's controlled record for the designated intake joint R.
Joint R is a named location in this procedure, not a general component
taxonomy or a physical-topology subgraph.

A complete record identifies the same job, the same reproduced complaint
and profile RP-IDLE, no other diagnostic changes, and all four observations:

| Observation | Fictional criterion |
| --- | --- |
| A: original configuration | Recorded correction exceeds +15% |
| B: joint R isolated in the workshop comparison | Recorded correction is between -5% and +5%, inclusive |
| A2: original configuration restored | Recorded correction again exceeds +15% |
| C: comparison control at joint K, with R in its original configuration | Recorded correction exceeds +15% |

Here "correction" is the percentage field explicitly identified in the
workshop report. These invented bands define only this source's category.
Do not substitute a different percentage field, operating profile or job.

If all four criteria are met and pressure remains within its reference band
throughout the comparison, take the repeatable-localisation result to G2.4.
A separately signed pressure-stability statement for the comparison is
acceptable; pressure values need not be repeated in every row.

If the completed, otherwise valid record fails to reproduce the pattern,
take the non-localising result to the workshop-review action in G2.5.
If a required observation or control is missing, the supplied record is
incomplete: clarify at this action rather than treating it as non-localising.
If the record explicitly says the entire comparison was not done, leave this
review as the next action.

A single improvement in B is not enough. In particular, a low correction
that remains low after restoring A does not localise the fault to R.

nodes.description: Review the current RP-IDLE pressure record
nodes.instruction:
## G2.2 Review the current pressure record

The next action is to review the saved workshop pressure record for profile
RP-IDLE: the current complaint reproduced at running idle for the declared
job. A valid record identifies that profile, the job, the value and the unit.

For this fictional profile only, the reference band is 550 through 700 kPa,
including both boundaries. The documented unit conversion is 1 bar = 100 kPa;
therefore a correctly scoped 6.25 bar record means 625 kPa.
Do not invent a unit for "6.25" or apply an undocumented conversion.

| Recorded result | Permitted transition |
| --- | --- |
| A complete current RP-IDLE record is inside the inclusive band | Continue to the localisation-record review in G2.3 |
| A complete current RP-IDLE record is outside the band | Request workshop review of the out-of-band pressure finding; no component cause is established |
| No pressure record has been supplied or the check was not done | Stop with this pressure-record review as the next action |
| A supplied record lacks the unit or profile, or equally applicable records conflict | Clarify at this action |

An old low reading, a crossed-out value or a measurement taken in a different
operating profile does not override the applicable RP-IDLE record. Conversely,
do not discard two conflicting applicable records merely by choosing the
more convenient value. Ask the workshop to resolve the conflict.

Being inside the reference band does not prove that the vehicle has no fault.
It only permits the next published action in this guide.

Use only records for the declared vehicle, current job and requested profile. A supplied wrong-vehicle record requires clarification, not a result.

nodes.instruction:
## G2.3 Review the controlled localisation record

This action is available after the current pressure record is within band.
It reviews the workshop's controlled record for the designated intake joint S.
Joint S is a named location in this procedure, not a general component
taxonomy or a physical-topology subgraph.

A complete record identifies the same job, the same reproduced complaint
and profile RP-IDLE, no other diagnostic changes, and all four observations:

| Observation | Fictional criterion |
| --- | --- |
| A: original configuration | Recorded correction exceeds +15% |
| B: joint S isolated in the workshop comparison | Recorded correction is between -5% and +5%, inclusive |
| A2: original configuration restored | Recorded correction again exceeds +15% |
| C: comparison control at joint K, with S in its original configuration | Recorded correction exceeds +15% |

Here "correction" is the percentage field explicitly identified in the
workshop report. These invented bands define only this source's category.
Do not substitute a different percentage field, operating profile or job.

If all four criteria are met and pressure remains within its reference band
throughout the comparison, take the repeatable-localisation result to G2.4.
A separately signed pressure-stability statement for the comparison is
acceptable; pressure values need not be repeated in every row.

If the completed, otherwise valid record fails to reproduce the pattern,
take the non-localising result to the workshop-review action in G2.5.
If a required observation or control is missing, the supplied record is
incomplete: clarify at this action rather than treating it as non-localising.
If the record explicitly says the entire comparison was not done, leave this
review as the next action.

A single improvement in B is not enough. In particular, a low correction
that remains low after restoring A does not localise the fault to S.

nodes.description: Review the current RP-IDLE pressure record
nodes.instruction:
## G2.2 Review the current pressure record

The next action is to review the saved workshop pressure record for profile
RP-IDLE: the current complaint reproduced at running idle for the declared
job. A valid record identifies that profile, the job, the value and the unit.

For this fictional profile only, the reference band is 225 through 325 kPa,
including both boundaries. The documented unit conversion is 1 bar = 100 kPa;
therefore a correctly scoped 2.75 bar record means 275 kPa.
Do not invent a unit for "2.75" or apply an undocumented conversion.

| Recorded result | Permitted transition |
| --- | --- |
| A complete current RP-IDLE record is inside the inclusive band | Continue to the localisation-record review in G2.3 |
| A complete current RP-IDLE record is outside the band | Request workshop review of the out-of-band pressure finding; no component cause is established |
| No pressure record has been supplied or the check was not done | Stop with this pressure-record review as the next action |
| A supplied record lacks the unit or profile, or equally applicable records conflict | Clarify at this action |

An old low reading, a crossed-out value or a measurement taken in a different
operating profile does not override the applicable RP-IDLE record. Conversely,
do not discard two conflicting applicable records merely by choosing the
more convenient value. Ask the workshop to resolve the conflict.

Being inside the reference band does not prove that the vehicle has no fault.
It only permits the next published action in this guide.

Use only records for the declared vehicle, current job and requested profile. A supplied wrong-vehicle record requires clarification, not a result.

nodes.instruction:
## G2.3 Review the controlled localisation record

This action is available after the current pressure record is within band.
It reviews the workshop's controlled record for the designated intake joint T.
Joint T is a named location in this procedure, not a general component
taxonomy or a physical-topology subgraph.

A complete record identifies the same job, the same reproduced complaint
and profile RP-IDLE, no other diagnostic changes, and all four observations:

| Observation | Fictional criterion |
| --- | --- |
| A: original configuration | Recorded correction exceeds +15% |
| B: joint T isolated in the workshop comparison | Recorded correction is between -5% and +5%, inclusive |
| A2: original configuration restored | Recorded correction again exceeds +15% |
| C: comparison control at joint K, with T in its original configuration | Recorded correction exceeds +15% |

Here "correction" is the percentage field explicitly identified in the
workshop report. These invented bands define only this source's category.
Do not substitute a different percentage field, operating profile or job.

If all four criteria are met and pressure remains within its reference band
throughout the comparison, take the repeatable-localisation result to G2.4.
A separately signed pressure-stability statement for the comparison is
acceptable; pressure values need not be repeated in every row.

If the completed, otherwise valid record fails to reproduce the pattern,
take the non-localising result to the workshop-review action in G2.5.
If a required observation or control is missing, the supplied record is
incomplete: clarify at this action rather than treating it as non-localising.
If the record explicitly says the entire comparison was not done, leave this
review as the next action.

A single improvement in B is not enough. In particular, a low correction
that remains low after restoring A does not localise the fault to T.

Use this guide when the complaint concerns air not leaving the cabin vents,
or airflow missing at one or more fan stages. A customer may call this
"the air-con has stopped", "the heater is dead" or "it only works flat out".
Those phrases do not establish a component fault.

If it is unclear whether the complaint is missing airflow or the temperature
of air that is flowing normally, ask that question before claiming an entry.
This guide does not diagnose refrigerant, heating or cooling performance.

## G4.0 Provenance, applicability and precedence

This supplement extends SG-01, SG-02 and SG-03 to the ten configurations below.
It is authored fictional guidance, not manufacturer information or expert-
validated advice. All numbers, protocols and component findings are invented.
Review supplied workshop records only; do not perform vehicle work.

Each row is an exact applicability boundary, not a family-wide approval.
The original three guides remain unchanged for row a21. For the other rows,
use the base guide's evidence controls with this supplement's explicit
substitutions and ordering. Never transfer a pressure band, cylinder finding,
review order or fan-stage pattern from a neighbouring configuration.
No priorities between simultaneous current misfire and lean findings are given.

Model, year and configuration must be established. Missing identity requires
clarification even if the catalogue currently lists only one matching model.
An explicitly unsupported configuration is unsupported, not the nearest match.
If a selected vehicle and the report disagree, clarify the conflict rather than
silently choosing either one. A missing selection does not establish identity.
Vehicle/job/profile identifiers on workshop records must match the current case.
Historical or explicitly different-vehicle records cannot establish a transition.

nodes.description: Review the current workshop fan-stage record
nodes.instruction:
## G4.6 Vehicle-specific fan-stage review

Review the current workshop record for all four commanded fan stages.
Customer language may establish an airflow complaint, not a completed check.
For this vehicle, airflow absent at stages 1-3 and present at
stages 4 permits the CP-FAN control-unit comparison.
No airflow at any stage requires complete-loss referral. Airflow at every
stage with a temperature-only complaint is outside this diagnostic scope.
Any other complete pattern requires unhandled-pattern referral, not an
invented component finding. No workshop record leaves this review as the
next action. A partial or contradictory supplied record requires clarification.

Use only records for the declared vehicle, current job and requested profile. A supplied wrong-vehicle record requires clarification, not a result.

nodes.instruction:
## G4.7 Vehicle-specific control-unit comparison

Review the complete current-job CP-FAN record. Supply, ground and connection
checks must explicitly meet CP-FAN requirements throughout. The low-speed
control unit must be the only changed diagnostic variable.
A: original unit, no airflow at 1-3, airflow at 4.
B: reference unit, airflow at all four stages.
A2: original restored, the same 1-3/4 pattern recurs.
Only this complete controlled pattern establishes the original low-speed
fan control-unit fault. A complete otherwise valid non-localising comparison
requires referral. No comparison leaves this review as the next action.
Partial return records, missing prerequisites or conflicting unit identities
require clarification. A single improvement does not establish a cause.

Use only records for the declared vehicle, current job and requested profile. A supplied wrong-vehicle record requires clarification, not a result.

nodes.title: Rough running with a current cylinder-four misfire finding
nodes.entry_criteria:
## G1.1 Entry and distinction from other guidance

Use this procedure when rough running is accompanied by a current scan
recording the exact code P0304. That finding establishes a cylinder-four
misfire report; it does not establish a failed ignition component.

Rough idle or a warning light alone does not distinguish this procedure from
[SG-02](SG-02-lean-idle.md). Ask for the current scan finding before selecting
between them. A historical P0171 report does not override a current P0304
record. P03040 is not P0304.

If both P0304 and P0171 are current, these three guides do not establish which
procedure takes priority. Clarify with the workshop; do not assume code
priority or claim that one code explains the other.

If the symptom or current finding is different, do not force it into this
procedure. Request clarification or report that the supplied guides do not
cover the established complaint.

## G4.0 Provenance, applicability and precedence

This supplement extends SG-01, SG-02 and SG-03 to the ten configurations below.

validated advice. All numbers, protocols and component findings are invented.
Review supplied workshop records only; do not perform vehicle work.

use the base guide's evidence controls with this supplement's explicit
substitutions and ordering. Never transfer a pressure band, cylinder finding,
review order or fan-stage pattern from a neighbouring configuration.
No priorities between simultaneous current misfire and lean findings are given.

Model, year and configuration must be established. Missing identity requires
clarification even if the catalogue currently lists only one matching model.
An explicitly unsupported configuration is unsupported, not the nearest match.
If a selected vehicle and the report disagree, clarify the conflict rather than
silently choosing either one. A missing selection does not establish identity.
Vehicle/job/profile identifiers on workshop records must match the current case.
Historical or explicitly different-vehicle records cannot establish a transition.

## G4.2 Misfire variants

For each configuration the exact entry code is P030 followed by its cylinder
number. The donor code is P030 followed by its donor number. The base guide's
"cylinder one" references mean the scheduled cylinder instead. Exact code
matching still applies: an extra digit is not the same finding.

Coil-first rows use SG-01's order: coil review, then plug review only if the
complete coil comparison leaves the misfire on the original cylinder.
Plug-first rows instead use the review instructions in G4.3 and G4.4.
The first comparison following the component with a valid return establishes
that component finding. If it remains on the original cylinder, review the
second component. If both complete comparisons remain on that cylinder,
refer for unresolved misfire; do not invent another component conclusion.
Never reuse controls from one comparison as evidence that the other was done.

nodes.instruction:
## G4.4 Coil review after a non-localising plug comparison

This review follows a complete plug-only comparison that remained on cylinder
4. Review a separate coil-only comparison for the current job:
baseline P0304, donor cylinder 3, plugs restored and unchanged,
only coils changed, observed cylinder and a return comparison.
If the result becomes P0303 and returning reproduces P0304,
the original cylinder-4 coil fault is established.
If the complete comparison remains P0304 during the exchange and
after return, refer for unresolved misfire. No coil record or a statement
that the check was not done leaves this review as the next action.
Partial, conflicting or inconclusive supplied evidence requires clarification.

nodes.description: Review the recorded plug comparison
nodes.instruction:
## G4.3 Plug-first entry review

Review the current job's recorded plug-only comparison for P0304,
original cylinder 4, donor cylinder 3. This is the FIRST review;
no earlier coil comparison is required. An interpretable record reproduces
P0304 at baseline, changes only the plugs between these cylinders,
identifies the resulting cylinder and records the return to original positions.
Coils and other diagnostic variables remain unchanged within this comparison.
If the result becomes P0303 and returning reproduces P0304,
the original cylinder-4 plug fault is established. If the complete
comparison remains P0304 during the exchange and after return,
continue to the coil review. If no comparison exists or it was not done,
leave this review as the next action. A supplied partial, conflicting or
inconclusive comparison requires clarification, not either result branch.

Use only records for the declared vehicle, current job and requested profile. A supplied wrong-vehicle record requires clarification, not a result.

## G4.5 Lean-mixture variants

For every scheduled vehicle SG-02's entry remains rough idle with current
P0171 and no competing current P030 code for that configuration.
Use its scheduled pressure limits instead of 250-400 kPa, including both
boundaries. The only documented conversion remains 1 bar = 100 kPa.
A declared unit, current job and RP-IDLE profile are required.
Inside the vehicle's band permits its scheduled joint-localisation review;
outside requires pressure referral, never a pump diagnosis.
Missing units, conflicting applicable values or a supplied wrong-vehicle
record require clarification at pressure review. No supplied pressure record
leaves pressure review as the next action.

The controlled localisation record has the same complete A/B/A2/C criteria as
SG-02: A >+15%, B between -5% and +5%, A2 >+15%, C >+15%;

vehicle's band throughout. Replace joint J with the scheduled joint;
the control remains joint K. The complete repeatable pattern establishes only
an unmetered-air leak at the scheduled joint. A complete non-localising record
requires referral; partial controls require clarification.

nodes.description: Review the current RP-IDLE pressure record
nodes.instruction:
## G2.2 Review the current pressure record

The next action is to review the saved workshop pressure record for profile
RP-IDLE: the current complaint reproduced at running idle for the declared
job. A valid record identifies that profile, the job, the value and the unit.

For this fictional profile only, the reference band is 475 through 625 kPa,
including both boundaries. The documented unit conversion is 1 bar = 100 kPa;
therefore a correctly scoped 5.5 bar record means 550 kPa.
Do not invent a unit for "5.5" or apply an undocumented conversion.

| Recorded result | Permitted transition |
| --- | --- |
| A complete current RP-IDLE record is inside the inclusive band | Continue to the localisation-record review in G2.3 |
| A complete current RP-IDLE record is outside the band | Request workshop review of the out-of-band pressure finding; no component cause is established |
| No pressure record has been supplied or the check was not done | Stop with this pressure-record review as the next action |
| A supplied record lacks the unit or profile, or equally applicable records conflict | Clarify at this action |

An old low reading, a crossed-out value or a measurement taken in a different
operating profile does not override the applicable RP-IDLE record. Conversely,
do not discard two conflicting applicable records merely by choosing the
more convenient value. Ask the workshop to resolve the conflict.

Being inside the reference band does not prove that the vehicle has no fault.
It only permits the next published action in this guide.

Use only records for the declared vehicle, current job and requested profile. A supplied wrong-vehicle record requires clarification, not a result.

nodes.description: The current RP-IDLE pressure record is within the source reference band.
Review the complete joint U localisation record
nodes.instruction:
## G2.3 Review the controlled localisation record

This action is available after the current pressure record is within band.
It reviews the workshop's controlled record for the designated intake joint U.
Joint U is a named location in this procedure, not a general component
taxonomy or a physical-topology subgraph.

A complete record identifies the same job, the same reproduced complaint
and profile RP-IDLE, no other diagnostic changes, and all four observations:

| Observation | Fictional criterion |
| --- | --- |
| A: original configuration | Recorded correction exceeds +15% |
| B: joint U isolated in the workshop comparison | Recorded correction is between -5% and +5%, inclusive |
| A2: original configuration restored | Recorded correction again exceeds +15% |
| C: comparison control at joint K, with U in its original configuration | Recorded correction exceeds +15% |

Here "correction" is the percentage field explicitly identified in the
workshop report. These invented bands define only this source's category.
Do not substitute a different percentage field, operating profile or job.

If all four criteria are met and pressure remains within its reference band
throughout the comparison, take the repeatable-localisation result to G2.4.
A separately signed pressure-stability statement for the comparison is
acceptable; pressure values need not be repeated in every row.

If the completed, otherwise valid record fails to reproduce the pattern,
take the non-localising result to the workshop-review action in G2.5.
If a required observation or control is missing, the supplied record is
incomplete: clarify at this action rather than treating it as non-localising.
If the record explicitly says the entire comparison was not done, leave this
review as the next action.

A single improvement in B is not enough. In particular, a low correction
that remains low after restoring A does not localise the fault to U.

Use only records for the declared vehicle, current job and requested profile. A supplied wrong-vehicle record requires clarification, not a result.

nodes.entry_criteria:
## G3.1 Entry and scope distinction

Use this guide when the complaint concerns air not leaving the cabin vents,
or airflow missing at one or more fan stages. A customer may call this
"the air-con has stopped", "the heater is dead" or "it only works flat out".
Those phrases do not establish a component fault.

If it is unclear whether the complaint is missing airflow or the temperature
of air that is flowing normally, ask that question before claiming an entry.
This guide does not diagnose refrigerant, heating or cooling performance.

## G4.0 Provenance, applicability and precedence

This supplement extends SG-01, SG-02 and SG-03 to the ten configurations below.
It is authored fictional guidance, not manufacturer information or expert-
validated advice. All numbers, protocols and component findings are invented.
Review supplied workshop records only; do not perform vehicle work.

Each row is an exact applicability boundary, not a family-wide approval.
The original three guides remain unchanged for row a21. For the other rows,
use the base guide's evidence controls with this supplement's explicit
substitutions and ordering. Never transfer a pressure band, cylinder finding,
review order or fan-stage pattern from a neighbouring configuration.
No priorities between simultaneous current misfire and lean findings are given.

Model, year and configuration must be established. Missing identity requires
clarification even if the catalogue currently lists only one matching model.
An explicitly unsupported configuration is unsupported, not the nearest match.
If a selected vehicle and the report disagree, clarify the conflict rather than
silently choosing either one. A missing selection does not establish identity.
Vehicle/job/profile identifiers on workshop records must match the current case.
Historical or explicitly different-vehicle records cannot establish a transition.

edges.selection_criteria: Complete current-job coil-only comparison: P0301 baseline; misfire follows the coil to the donor; return check reproduces P0301. All controls in G1.2 required.
edges.confirmation_basis:
## G1.2 Review the recorded coil comparison

At the entry state, the next action is to review the workshop's completed,
controlled ignition-coil comparison record.

An interpretable comparison identifies:

- The current job, the original P0301 finding and the donor cylinder.
- A baseline observation reproducing the original finding.
- A coil-only change, with the plug and other diagnostic variables unchanged.
- The observed cylinder after that change.
- A return-to-original comparison reproducing the baseline finding.

For this fictional guide, the published result categories are:

| Recorded result | Permitted transition |
| --- | --- |
| The misfire follows the cylinder-one coil to the donor cylinder, and returning the coils reproduces P0301 | Terminal finding in G1.4: cylinder-one ignition-coil fault |
| The misfire remains on cylinder one during a valid coil comparison and after the return check | Continue to the plug-record review in G1.3; a coil fault has not been established |
| No coil-comparison record is supplied, or the check was not done | Stop with the coil-record review as the next action |
| A supplied comparison lacks a required control or observation, or is inconclusive | Clarify at this action; do not take either result branch |
| Records of the same coil comparison disagree about what changed or which cylinder misfired | Clarify at this action; do not merge the records into a diagnosis |

The phrase "no change after substitution" is insufficient by itself. It must
be attributable to a coil-only comparison for this job with the required
controls. A parts recommendation or replacement invoice is not that evidence.

edges.selection_criteria: Valid current-job coil-only comparison: P0301 persists with coils exchanged and after return; plugs unchanged. A plug check need not have been done yet.
Complete plug-only comparison after the valid coil check: P0301 baseline; misfire follows the original plug to donor cylinder; returning plugs reproduces P0301; coils original throughout.
edges.confirmation_basis:
## G1.3 Review the recorded plug comparison

This action is available only after the valid coil comparison leaves the
misfire on cylinder one. A statement that the plug has not been checked means
this action remains outstanding, not that the plug passed or failed.

The plug comparison uses the same record requirements as G1.2, except that
the plug is the only changed diagnostic variable and the coils are in their
original positions. Its baseline must still reproduce P0301.

| Recorded result | Permitted transition |
| --- | --- |
| The misfire follows the cylinder-one plug to the donor cylinder, and returning the plugs reproduces P0301 | Terminal finding in G1.4: cylinder-one spark-plug fault |
| The misfire remains on cylinder one in the completed comparison | Continue to the workshop-review action in G1.5 |
| The record is not supplied or explicitly says the check was not done | Stop with the plug-record review as the next action |
| A supplied record is partial, contradictory or inconclusive | Clarify at the plug-record review |

edges.selection_criteria: Completed valid plug comparison leaves the misfire on cylinder one. Missing or incomplete comparisons are NOT this result.
Current job RP-IDLE record, declared unit, 250-400 kPa inclusive. Explicitly permitted conversion: 1 bar = 100 kPa. Old/key-on records are not applicable.
Complete current-job RP-IDLE record outside 250-400 kPa inclusive, with declared kPa or bar. A missing unit is clarification, not this result.
All complete same-job RP-IDLE records: A >+15%, B in [-5,+5]%, A2 >+15%, control C >+15%, no other diagnostic changes, pressure within band throughout.
edges.confirmation_basis:
## G2.3 Review the controlled localisation record

This action is available after the current pressure record is within band.
It reviews the workshop's controlled record for the designated intake joint J.
Joint J is a named location in this procedure, not a general component
taxonomy or a physical-topology subgraph.

A complete record identifies the same job, the same reproduced complaint
and profile RP-IDLE, no other diagnostic changes, and all four observations:

| Observation | Fictional criterion |
| --- | --- |
| A: original configuration | Recorded correction exceeds +15% |
| B: joint J isolated in the workshop comparison | Recorded correction is between -5% and +5%, inclusive |
| A2: original configuration restored | Recorded correction again exceeds +15% |
| C: comparison control at joint K, with J in its original configuration | Recorded correction exceeds +15% |

Here "correction" is the percentage field explicitly identified in the
workshop report. These invented bands define only this source's category.
Do not substitute a different percentage field, operating profile or job.

If all four criteria are met and pressure remains within its reference band
throughout the comparison, take the repeatable-localisation result to G2.4.
A separately signed pressure-stability statement for the comparison is
acceptable; pressure values need not be repeated in every row.

If the completed, otherwise valid record fails to reproduce the pattern,
take the non-localising result to the workshop-review action in G2.5.
If a required observation or control is missing, the supplied record is
incomplete: clarify at this action rather than treating it as non-localising.
If the record explicitly says the entire comparison was not done, leave this
review as the next action.

A single improvement in B is not enough. In particular, a low correction
that remains low after restoring A does not localise the fault to J.

edges.selection_criteria: All required current-job comparison observations and prerequisites supplied, but required pattern fails. In particular A2 of +4% fails recurrence. Missing A2 or C instead requires clarification.
Current WORKSHOP record: no airflow at 1,2,3; airflow present at 4. A customer complaint alone is not the workshop record.
Complete current workshop record: no airflow at any of 1,2,3,4.
Current workshop record: airflow at all stages; remaining complaint concerns air temperature.
Complete current workshop record with another speed pattern, not incomplete or contradictory.

Complete CP-FAN comparison: supply/ground/connection prerequisites pass throughout; only low-speed control unit changes; A original 1-3 absent/4 present, B reference all present, A2 original pattern recurs.
edges.confirmation_basis:
## G3.3 Review the low-speed control comparison

The next action is to review the workshop's completed controlled comparison.
For the fictional reference procedure CP-FAN, an interpretable record states:

- It concerns the same current job and reproduced fan-stage pattern.
- The workshop's supply, ground and connection-integrity checks met CP-FAN
  requirements throughout the comparison.
- The low-speed control unit was the only changed diagnostic variable.
- A: with the original unit, stages 1-3 have no airflow and stage 4 has airflow.
- B: with the reference unit, airflow is present at all four stages.
- A2: with the original unit restored, the original 1-3/4 pattern recurs.

CP-FAN is a fictional record-review protocol, not an electrical procedure.
This document supplies no real test limits or physical test instructions.
A report can state that its protocol checks passed; a model must not invent
that statement or infer it solely from the fan-stage pattern.

| Recorded result | Permitted transition |
| --- | --- |
| The complete comparison meets all criteria above | Terminal finding in G3.4 |
| A complete, otherwise valid comparison does not reproduce the A-B-A2 pattern | Request workshop review of unresolved low-speed airflow loss |
| The comparison was not done or no comparison record has been supplied | Leave this comparison-record review as the next action |
| A comparison is supplied but the return check, protocol prerequisites or another required observation is missing | Clarify at this action |
| Observations or the identity of the changed unit conflict | Clarify at this action |

Do not name a failed unit from B alone. The return comparison prevents a
single coincidental improvement from becoming the terminal conclusion.

edges.selection_criteria: Completed otherwise valid CP-FAN comparison fails the required A-B-A2 pattern. Missing return or prerequisite record instead requires clarification.

Take only the 'misfire follows coil' outcome under this complete review:

| Recorded result | Permitted transition |
| --- | --- |
| The misfire follows the cylinder-two coil to the donor cylinder, and returning the coils reproduces P0302 | Terminal finding in G1.4: cylinder-two ignition-coil fault |

| A supplied comparison lacks a required control or observation, or is inconclusive | Clarify at this action; do not take either result branch |
| Records of the same coil comparison disagree about what changed or which cylinder misfired | Clarify at this action; do not merge the records into a diagnosis |

be attributable to a coil-only comparison for this job with the required
controls. A parts recommendation or replacement invoice is not that evidence.

## G2.3 Review the controlled localisation record

This action is available after the current pressure record is within band.
It reviews the workshop's controlled record for the designated intake joint U.
Joint U is a named location in this procedure, not a general component
taxonomy or a physical-topology subgraph.

A complete record identifies the same job, the same reproduced complaint
and profile RP-IDLE, no other diagnostic changes, and all four observations:

| Observation | Fictional criterion |
| --- | --- |
| A: original configuration | Recorded correction exceeds +15% |
| B: joint U isolated in the workshop comparison | Recorded correction is between -5% and +5%, inclusive |
| A2: original configuration restored | Recorded correction again exceeds +15% |
| C: comparison control at joint K, with U in its original configuration | Recorded correction exceeds +15% |

Here "correction" is the percentage field explicitly identified in the
workshop report. These invented bands define only this source's category.
Do not substitute a different percentage field, operating profile or job.

If all four criteria are met and pressure remains within its reference band
throughout the comparison, take the repeatable-localisation result to G2.4.
A separately signed pressure-stability statement for the comparison is
acceptable; pressure values need not be repeated in every row.

If the completed, otherwise valid record fails to reproduce the pattern,
take the non-localising result to the workshop-review action in G2.5.
If a required observation or control is missing, the supplied record is
incomplete: clarify at this action rather than treating it as non-localising.
If the record explicitly says the entire comparison was not done, leave this
review as the next action.

A single improvement in B is not enough. In particular, a low correction
that remains low after restoring A does not localise the fault to U.
